conviction_note: The guide implies H2 growth of about 20% while sell-side Q3/Q4 consensus sits at or above the top of it. A beat-and-raise is the likely print (+4% vs bar), but this name sold two of its three beat-and-raise prints (-7.1%, -9.6%) and bought one (+21.1%). The reaction function vetoes most of the fundamental read: p_up 55 on an abs move of 9 gives +0.9, against an impact_sum of +1.8. Most of the gap is the large sell-off risk on good numbers, which the per-finding sizes do not carry.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $85.7M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/OMDA/earnings-forecasts) vs $87.39M from 9 analysts (FXEmpire, https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/omda/earnings). The two sources disagree by $1.7M. Company guide FY2026 revenue is $334-340M and adj. EBITDA $21-27M (raised 2026-08-06, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001611115/000162828026054266/q2fy26pressrelease.htm). H1 actual is $78M (Q1, https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/omada-health-reports-first-quarter-2026-results) + $87.8M (Q2), so the guide implies H2 revenue of about $168-174M, or $84-87M a quarter. Sell-side Q3 $85.7-87.4M plus Q4 $86.9M is about $173-174M, at the top of the guide. The bar is sourced to the company guide, so sizes are not capped; the EPS consensus is unresolved ($0.01 vs $0.08).
positioning_check: Short interest: 12.47% of float, 5.9 days to cover as of 2026-08-19 (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/omda/shortinterest); 7.98M shares, 17.11% of float, 6.72 days to cover at the mid-July 2026 settlement (Fintel, https://fintel.io/ss/us/omda). No October settlement was found; Nasdaq's API returned 503. That is a moderately crowded short. Skew is not available: the chain is unusable (ATM spread 120% of mid, total OI 505, put/call OI 1.9). ATM IV of 102.6% vs 20-day realised 79.8% with 15 days to expiry backs out an event SD of roughly 13-14%, and unusualwhales quotes +/-17.5% (https://unusualwhales.com/stock/OMDA/earnings). Both are unreliable. Tape: -6.4% over 5 days, -11.7% over 20 days, -26% from the 52-week high. Revelation Alpine (a former >5% holder) reported 0 shares as of 2026-09-30 (13G/A filed 2026-11-02); BlackRock reported a new 6.0% stake (13G, event 2026-09-30).

findings.finding: The raised FY2026 guide ($334-340M) implies H2 revenue of about $168-174M, roughly +20% YoY against 2H25's 54% growth. The company has beaten revenue consensus by 8.5% (Q2 2026: $87.8M vs $80.9M) and 11% (Q3 2025: $68M vs $61.2M). Last year's H2 sequential growth was +11% (Q2->Q3) and +12% (Q3->Q4), while Q3 2026 consensus of $85.7-87.4M implies flat-to-down from Q2's $87.8M. A Q3 print of about $89-92M (+4% vs bar) and a further FY raise is the likely outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Real prints since the 2025 IPO, checked: Q2'25 (2025-08-07) -2.3%. Q3'25 (2025-11-06): 11% beat and raise, -7.1%. Q4'25 (2026-03-05) +3.3%; it was pre-announced 2026-01-12, which moved +4.6%. Q1'26 (2026-05-07): beat and raise, -9.6%. Q2'26 (2026-08-06): 8.5% beat and raise, +21.1%. Beat-and-raise has been sold twice and bought once.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side numbers already sit at the top of the guide, so a modest beat is partly expected. A sequential step up to the $90M+ that last year's H2 seasonality points to is not in the $85.7-87.4M consensus. If it were priced, consensus would carry sequential growth and the stock would not be -12% over 20 days into the print.
findings.independence: Q2 call commentary (TipRanks, 2026-08-08, https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/omada-health-earnings-call-highlights-profitable-surge) says management expects slower H2 growth on seasonality (Q1 is the strongest enrollment quarter), which argues for conservatism being partly real. Consensus figures: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/OMDA/earnings-forecasts. The guide and the beat history come from company documents; the H2 sequential pattern is an inference.

findings.finding: Hinge Health, the closest employer-channel digital-health peer, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-02, three days after Omada last spoke publicly: revenue +52% to $235.0M, FY guide raised to $879-881M, clients +28% to 3,270, and the CEO cited 'a record sales season'. That is a read-through for employer demand in the January 2027 benefit cycle, which Omada's own call said is closed in H2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior OMDA print has been measured against a same-week Hinge read-through. OMDA fell 6.4% in the 5 sessions spanning Hinge's raise, so this read-through has not been rewarded so far.
findings.why_not_priced: OMDA traded down through the Hinge print rather than up, so the market has not carried the employer-selling-season read across to Omada. If it had, OMDA's 5-day run-up would be positive, not -6.4%.
findings.independence: This is a proxy (different condition category, MSK vs cardiometabolic). Omada's own Q2 call (TipRanks, 2026-08-08) framed H2 as the closing season for January launches, which is the same mechanism. Hinge 8-K exhibit: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001673743/000162828026068872/hnge-q32026112xex991.htm (same document).

findings.finding: On the Q2 call, management said the Q2 adj. EBITDA margin (about 12%) is above what it expects for H2 as earlier hiring annualizes, with opex flat to up and margin lower sequentially. The FY $21-27M guide less H1's ~$12M ($1M + $11M) leaves $9-15M for H2, so Q3 adj. EBITDA of roughly $4-8M is the guided path, down from $11M in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history isolates a margin step-down. Q1'26 adj. EBITDA was $1M with a 62% gross margin, and the stock fell 9.6% despite a raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it sits inside the company guide. The risk is that a headline Q3 EBITDA well below Q2's $11M reads as deterioration to a less careful audience. If that were fully priced, consensus EPS would be clustered near zero; it ranges from $0.01 to $0.08.
findings.independence: Same guide document as finding 1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001611115/000162828026054266/q2fy26pressrelease.htm); not independent of it.

findings.finding: Revelation Alpine, LLC, which had converted options into about 4.18M shares and was a >5% holder, filed a 13G/A on 2026-11-02 reporting 0 shares (0.0%) as of 2026-09-30. BlackRock filed a new 13G on 2026-10-27 reporting 3,667,682 shares (6.0%) as of the same date. A large holder's exit is complete before the print.
findings.why_not_priced: The 13G/A was filed three days before the print and is not in any preview. The exit happened by 9/30 and the stock still fell 16% from $21.87 (Oct 12) to $18.39, so October's weakness was not this holder's supply. If the market had read the overhang as gone, the post-exit tape would have firmed.
findings.independence: BlackRock 13G (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1611115/000201238326003824/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml, filed 2026-10-27) shows a long-only holder absorbing a similar block. That is a different filer and a different document.

findings.finding: Employer GLP-1 drug coverage is being pared for 2027: in the Business Group on Health survey only 72% of the 67% of employers that cover GLP-1s for weight said they are likely to continue, and Mercer reports 27% tightening and 5% considering dropping. Omada's management flagged GLP-1 coverage uncertainty as an H2 risk; GLP-1 track members were about 150k, under 20% of members.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print has turned on GLP-1 coverage commentary specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the surveys date from June. What is not priced is how Omada's 2027 selling-season commentary handles it. Omada's GLP-1 Flex Care (March 2026) and Lilly Employer Connect (May 2026) are built for employers that do not cover the drug, so the sign is ambiguous.
findings.independence: TipRanks Q2 call summary (https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/omada-health-earnings-call-highlights-profitable-surge) records management naming GLP-1 coverage as a risk. Macro-to-company transmission is not confirmed by the company with a number.

findings.finding: Short interest was 12.5-17.1% of float with 5.9-6.7 days to cover (July/August settlements), and the stock went into the print down 11.7% over 20 days and 26% off its 52-week high, with no company-specific news found for the October decline. That is a moderately crowded short into a name with a history of beat-and-raise prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 (+21.1%) came off a depressed base after Q1's -9.6%. The same setup squeezed once.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public. The squeeze is a mechanism only if the print beats, so this is conditional and small. An unexplained drawdown by itself is worth 0.
findings.independence: Equibles 2026-08-19 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/omda/shortinterest) gives 12.47% of float and 5.9 days, a different denominator and the same direction.

findings.finding: Form 144 filed 2026-11-04 for a proposed insider sale, the latest in a roughly monthly cadence of 144s and Form 4s since August (8/7, 8/10-12, 9/1, 9/9-10, 10/1, 11/4). This looks like routine 10b5-1 selling, not a signal.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial and routine. The cadence matches prior months, so it says nothing new.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001611115&type=144&dateb=&owner=include&count=5) shows the monthly pattern.

outside_window.finding: CEO transition: President Wei-Li Shao becomes CEO and co-founder Sean Duffy becomes Executive Chair on 2027-01-01. Any first-guide conservatism under the new CEO lands with the 2027 guide in early 2027, not this print.

searched_and_found_nothing: Cause of the October 2026 decline ($21.87 on Oct 12 to $18.39): MarketBeat and AAII automated price write-ups give no cause, and no downgrade was found (one upgrade in the month to Oct 9).

Investor Day (2026-09-10) reaction and any 2027 commentary: only the long-term targets were found (20%+ revenue growth, 80% non-GAAP GM, 30% adj. EBITDA margin; https://briefglance.com/companies/omada-health-inc/pulses/77185).

baseline_tension: The evidence leans mildly positive, against a -11.7% 20-day run-up and a 1.9 put/call OI ratio (no usable skew). A depressed price with a moderate short is the setup that paid +21% last quarter, but this name has also sold two beat-and-raise prints, so p_up only moves to 55.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): beat-and-raise was sold twice and bought once, so the beat/guide finding went from +1.5 to +1.0 and p_up from 56 to 55.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the positioning/drawdown finding went from +0.5 to +0.2; only the conditional squeeze mechanism is left.
Rule 6 (a finding inside the company guide moves toward 0): the H2 margin step-down went from -0.3 to -0.1.
Rule 5 (a proxy is sized small): the GLP-1 coverage proxy went from -0.3 to -0.2 and the Hinge read-through from +0.6 to +0.5.
Revelation Alpine exit: +0.5 to +0.4 (a document fact, but its effect on price is an inference).
Rule 8 and the core: abs_move_pct was left at 9 (real-print median about 7.1, mean about 8.7, IV-implied event SD about 13%), not shrunk.
